# lv24-opencode-consilium

[![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/lv24-opencode-consilium?label=npm&color=cb3837&logo=npm)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/lv24-opencode-consilium)
[![downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dm/lv24-opencode-consilium?color=cb3837)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/lv24-opencode-consilium)
[![GHCR](https://img.shields.io/badge/GHCR-ghcr.io%2Flevapveeskela%2Flv24--opencode--consilium-2496ED?logo=docker&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/LevapVeeskela/lv24-opencode-consilium/pkgs/container/lv24-opencode-consilium)

**Languages:** English · [Русский](docs/README.ru.md) · [中文](docs/README.zh.md)

> **Four experts. Four models. One plan.** Consilium runs `arch`, `ux`, `ba` and `sec` in parallel on different models, then a chair model merges their answers into a single actionable plan. Works inside OpenCode, Claude Desktop, Codex, Cursor, VS Code, CI and your own agents.

> **Кратко по-русски.** Консилиум ИИ-экспертов для OpenCode V1 и V2: роли `arch`, `ux`, `ba`, `sec` параллельно отвечают на разных моделях, а председатель синтезирует итоговый план. Бесплатные модели подбираются и проверяются автоматически (`consilium init --free`). В комплекте: CLI, MCP-сервер, нативный плагин V2, артефакты запусков с replay/diff, анализ согласия, HTML/PR-отчёты, watch-режим и git-hooks.
>
> Установка: `npm install -g lv24-opencode-consilium`, затем `consilium doctor` и `consilium "ваша задача"`. Полная документация — [docs/README.ru.md](docs/README.ru.md).

## See it work

```bash
$ consilium "Review the authentication design"

  arch  → flint-40b-free          architecture, trade-offs
  ux    → inkling-2-small-free    flows, error states
  ba    → deepseek-v4.1-flash-free  scope, edge cases
  sec   → iceman-free             threats, authz, abuse

  chair → beam-free               ← synthesizes one plan
  ✓ 4 experts in parallel · free models · no API bill
```

The chair does not summarize — it resolves disagreements, drops weak points and returns one plan with explicit trade-offs. Every expert runs on its own model, so blind spots do not overlap.

## Why consilium

- **Different models = different blind spots.** One model misses what another catches; the chair makes the conflict explicit instead of averaging it away.
- **Zero cost by default.** Discovers free, tool-capable models from public catalogs, ranks them, verifies they actually answer in your region, and writes them into your config.
- **Uses what you already have.** OpenCode CLI does auth, providers and agents — no parallel provider stack, no extra keys.
- **Same engine everywhere.** Terminal, MCP server for any harness, native V2 plugin, library API.

## What you get

| | Feature | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 🧠 | **Parallel council** | Per-expert `agent` + `model`, bounded concurrency, isolated sessions |
| 🪑 | **Chair synthesis** | Configurable prompt template, per-expert text limits, usage and cost accounting |
| 🆓 | **Free-model bootstrap** | `models.dev` + OpenRouter + curated offline list, cached 12 h, optional live probe |
| 🩺 | **`doctor` preflight** | CLI version, config flavor, agents, models, MCP shape, V1/V2 pitfalls |
| 🧾 | **Run artifacts** | `run.json`, `report.md`, `experts/*.md`; `--replay` and `--diff-runs` |
| 📊 | **Reports** | Self-contained HTML, GitHub-ready PR markdown, SARIF 2.1.0, Jira/Linear tickets |
| 🔁 | **Watch mode** | Rerun on file changes with debounce, current git diff appended |
| 🪝 | **Git pre-commit hook** | Reviews staged changes and blocks the commit on failure |
| 🔌 | **MCP server** | stdio JSON-RPC with run, model, doctor and read-only artifact tools |
| 🧩 | **V2 plugin** | `consilium.run` tool inside the OpenCode V2 TUI |
| 🛡 | **Safe review** | `--read-only` denies writes/shell/MCP tools; `--isolate` uses per-agent worktrees |
| 🔒 | **Safe runner** | Prompt via stdin (no shell injection), `--standalone`, retries, timeouts, cost cap |
| 📦 | **Small and strict** | Zero runtime dependencies, TypeScript strict, Node >= 18 |

## Meet the council

| Role | Agent name | Looks at | Typical questions |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 🏛 | `arch` | Architecture and trade-offs | What breaks at 10× load? Which boundary is wrong? |
| 🎨 | `ux` | Flows, API ergonomics, error states | What does the user see on failure? Is this obvious? |
| 📋 | `ba` | Requirements and scope | What is out of scope? Which edge case is unowned? |
| 🛡 | `sec` | Threats, authz, abuse | Who can call this? What leaks? How is it rate-limited? |
| ⚖️ | `consilium` | Chair | Merges answers, resolves conflicts, returns one plan |

Want fewer voices? `-e arch,sec`, `--smart-experts` (heuristic role pick) or a preset.

## Install

```bash
npm install -g lv24-opencode-consilium

# or run without installing
npx -y lv24-opencode-consilium --help

# or install the thin Python launcher from PyPI (still needs Node.js + OpenCode)
pip install lv24-opencode-consilium
```

`pip` installs `consilium` and `consilium-mcp` console scripts that delegate to the npm package via `npx`; npm remains the canonical distribution. Python 3.9+ is required for the launcher. Details: [`docs/pypi.md`](docs/pypi.md).

**Requirements**

| Need | Details |
| --- | --- |
| Node.js | **>= 18** |
| OpenCode CLI | `npm install -g opencode-ai`, authenticated, **V1 or V2** |
| Optional | `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` for OpenRouter's free models |

### Container image (GHCR)

A self-contained image (Node.js, OpenCode CLI, `git`) for `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`:

```bash
docker pull ghcr.io/levapveeskela/lv24-opencode-consilium:1.12.1   # or :latest
docker run --rm ghcr.io/levapveeskela/lv24-opencode-consilium:latest --version
# consilium v1.12.1
```

Run it on a project — mount credentials and config, keep the project writable:

```bash
docker run --rm -it \
  -v "$PWD:/workspace" \
  -v "$HOME/.local/share/opencode:/home/node/.local/share/opencode" \
  -v "$HOME/.config/opencode:/home/node/.config/opencode:ro" \
  -u "$(id -u):$(id -g)" \
  ghcr.io/levapveeskela/lv24-opencode-consilium:latest \
  "Design a rate limiter for a public API"
```

The entrypoint is `consilium`, so every flag works (`doctor`, `init --free`, `models`, `mcp`). For the MCP server use `--entrypoint consilium-mcp`. Inside the image `HOME=/home/node`; config mounts to `/home/node/.config/opencode`, credentials to `/home/node/.local/share/opencode`. On Windows omit `-u` and use `%CD%` / `%USERPROFILE%` in `-v`.

## Quick start

```bash
# 1. Check the environment: CLI, config, agents, models
consilium doctor

# 2. Pick the strongest working free models and write the config
consilium init --free

# 3. Run the council
consilium "Design a rate limiter for a public API"
```

`init --free`:

1. downloads `https://models.dev/api.json` and `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models`;
2. keeps only free (`cost = 0`), active, chat models with tool calling and >= 32K context;
3. ranks them and probes the top candidates with a tiny real request (unless `--no-verify`);
4. writes the winners into `opencode.json` (agents `arch`, `ux`, `ba`, `sec`, `consilium`) and `consilium.config.json`;
5. never overwrites existing agent models unless you pass `--force`.

```bash
consilium init --free --dry-run      # preview, write nothing
consilium init --free --native-v2    # native V2 agents (agents + system)
```

## Works on OpenCode V1 and V2

Both branches are supported and the config shape is detected automatically.

| Area | OpenCode V1 | OpenCode V2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `opencode.json` agents | `agent` + `prompt` | `agents` + `system` |
| MCP servers | `mcp.<name>` + `enabled` | `mcp.servers.<name>` + `disabled` |
| Commands | `command` + `subtask` | `commands` + `subagent` |
| Agent model on `run --agent` | applied from config | **ignored**, `--model` required |

- **V1 shape is the safe default** — both versions read it, so `init --free` writes it.
- **Native V2 agents** only with `--native-v2` or when the file already uses V2 keys.
- **Models are always passed via `--model`**, so V2 cannot silently fall back to the root model.
- **Agents are read from both sections**, including `.opencode/opencode.json(c)` and parent directories.
- `RATE_LIMITED` retries short limits (up to 30 s) and fails fast with the retry delay for long ones.
- `doctor` reports CLI major, config flavor, `agent`/`agents` duplicates, dead V2 fields and flat MCP entries.

One-command MCP registration:

```bash
consilium mcp --install            # ./opencode.json
consilium mcp --install --global   # ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json
opencode mcp list                  # verify
```

## Context pack (`--context auto`)

Experts normally see only the task and the diff. `--context auto` adds the changed files, project rules, related tests and recent commits:

```bash
consilium --context auto --diff "Review the current changes"
```

Priority and budget: rules → changed files → related tests → commits; 48k chars total, 12k per file, 20 files. Binary, lock and generated files are skipped; every section is wrapped in `<untrusted-*>` markers so repo text cannot masquerade as instructions. `--context off` (default) keeps the old behavior.

## Free models, automatically

```bash
consilium models                 # top 20 ranked models
consilium models --available     # only providers you can use
consilium models --verify        # probe the shown models with a real request
consilium models --refresh       # ignore the 12 h cache
consilium models --json          # machine-readable
```

| Source | What it gives |
| --- | --- |
| `https://models.dev/api.json` | Full catalog, cost/limits/capabilities, links to paid siblings |
| `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models` | `:free` variants, context, `tools` support, expiry |
| Built-in curated list | Known-good OpenCode free models if a catalog rotates them out |

Cache: `%TEMP%/lv24-opencode-consilium/models-cache.json` (or `CONSILIUM_MODELS_CACHE`), TTL 12 h.

The `opencode-go` provider is not excluded wholesale: its free models (`*-free`, `iceman-contributor-free`, …) take part in ranking. Paid models such as `opencode-go/muse-spark-1.3-contributor` are not selected by `--free`; set them manually in `experts[].model` or `chair.model`.

Current recommended set (catalog as of 2026-11-08):

| Role | Model | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| arch | `opencode/flint-40b-free` | coding agent, structured output, 262k |
| ux | `opencode/inkling-2-small-free` | 1M context, multimodal, fast |
| ba | `opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free` | reasoning + agentic coding, 200k |
| sec | `opencode/iceman-free` | newest reasoning model, 262k (stealth) |
| chair | `opencode/beam-free` | top score, 1M, structured, coding/agentic |

Free models rotate: `init --free` re-checks the catalog and real responses. Stealth/alpha models (`iceman`, `crouton`) can disappear — `--refresh` picks replacements.

Ranking (0–1.2) is deterministic: context window 30%, tool calling 20%, structured output 10%, reasoning 10%, recency 10%, output limit 10%, family prior 10%, paid-sibling "shadow price" 15%, plus alpha/preview/stealth penalties.

Call outcomes are remembered in `.consilium/reliability.json` (successes, rate limits, timeouts, latency per model). `consilium models --reliability` prints the table; the ranking accepts an optional reliability bonus once a model has at least 3 attempts. The file is local and safe to delete.

## Local and privacy mode

Run only on local providers (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, vLLM):

```bash
consilium models --local              # only local models in the ranked catalog
consilium models --probe-local        # are Ollama / LM Studio running?
consilium init --local                # probe and write a localOnly config
consilium init --local --dry-run      # show the assignment without writing
consilium --local-only "Review the changes"
```

`init --local` asks Ollama (`/api/tags`) and LM Studio (`/v1/models`) for their model lists, assigns models round-robin to `arch`, `ux`, `ba`, `sec` and the chair, and writes `consilium.config.json` with `localOnly: true` (refuses to overwrite without `--force`).

`--local-only` is a hard guarantee: every expert and the chair must have an explicit model whose provider is local, otherwise the run is rejected before spawning (exit 2, MCP tool error, or a library error). A missing model is an error, not an implicit cloud fallback. `doctor` adds a `local-providers` check that fails when `localOnly` is on and no local provider is reachable.

## Use it from any harness (MCP)

```bash
consilium mcp          # stdio server
consilium-mcp          # same, direct binary
```

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "consilium": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "lv24-opencode-consilium", "mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

**Codex** (`~/.codex/config.toml`):

```toml
[mcp_servers.consilium]
command = "npx"
args = ["-y", "lv24-opencode-consilium", "mcp"]
```

**1.11.0** — read-only and isolated runs, MCP artifact tools, ticket reports and a larger eval corpus. `--read-only` restricts experts and the chair to read/glob/grep through a temporary `.opencode/opencode.json` layer with lock, backup and byte-exact restore; `audit` and the GitHub Action are read-only by default, and `--allow-write` opts out. `--isolate` runs each agent in an OpenCode worktree. MCP gains `consilium_list_runs`, `consilium_get_run`, `consilium_sarif` and `consilium_diff_runs`; `--report jira|linear` renders Jira wiki/Linear Markdown. V1 `tools`/`permission` now migrate to ordered V2 rules. The eval corpus grows to 22 fixtures; benchmark numbers are generated by a real run, not committed. 561 JavaScript tests + 9 Python tests.

**1.10.0** — PyPI distribution and SARIF upload in the GitHub Action. `pip install lv24-opencode-consilium` installs a thin, dependency-free `consilium` launcher that delegates to the npm CLI via `npx` (Node.js >= 18 and OpenCode remain prerequisites; npm stays canonical). PyPI publishing uses Trusted Publishing (OIDC) from `.github/workflows/pypi-publish.yml`, so a GitHub release publishes npm and PyPI without tokens or OTP. `consilium sarif --run <id|latest> [--output <file>]` exports SARIF from saved artifacts without re-running the council; the composite action now passes `--artifacts`, exports SARIF and uploads it with `github/codeql-action/upload-sarif` (`sarif`, `sarif-file`, `category` inputs; `security-events: write` required), and SARIF failures never mask the gate. 522 JavaScript tests + 5 Python tests.

**1.9.0** — SARIF export, debate evaluation and scheduler recipes. `--report sarif` emits SARIF 2.1.0 (severity mapping, file/line locations, stable fingerprints, rule ids per category) for GitHub code scanning and other SARIF viewers; `.sarif`/`.sarif.json` extensions are inferred. `eval --compare-rounds` runs every fixture with one and two rounds and prints catch/FP/p50/cost deltas; `eval --rounds 2` runs the suite in debate mode. `docs/scheduling.md` plus cron, Task Scheduler, launchd and GitHub Actions examples make commit-range audits schedulable without a daemon. 515 tests.

**1.8.0** — debate rounds, local bootstrap and commit-range audits. `--rounds 2` adds an anonymized peer-review round: each expert critiques the others and states a final position; the chair sees the final positions plus which experts changed, and `metadata.debate` records participants and changes. `consilium init --local` probes Ollama/LM Studio, assigns local models round-robin to every role and the chair, and writes a `localOnly` config. `consilium audit --since <ref>` reviews a commit range end-to-end, reusing reports, artifacts and `--fail-on`; `--dry-run` prints the request without model calls. 491 tests.

**1.7.0** — deadlines and privacy. `--deadline <ms>` caps the expert phase: stragglers are cancelled, the chair synthesizes the finished experts with a missing-roles note, and a run with zero completed experts fails with `DEADLINE`. `--local-only` requires an explicit local model (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, vLLM) for every agent; `models --local` filters the catalog and `models --probe-local` reports whether local providers are running; `doctor` adds a `local-providers` check. Custom presets in `consilium.config.json` merge over built-ins and work in CLI, MCP and the plugin (`consilium presets` lists them). The trusted-config marker now survives object spreads. 446 tests.

**1.6.0** — evaluation harness, context pack, reliability memory and a GitHub Action. `consilium eval` runs planted-bug fixtures with deterministic claim matching and reports catch/FP/p50 latency/cost (`--fail-under` exits `3`). `--context auto` adds changed files, the nearest `AGENTS.md`, related tests and recent commits under a char budget. Model outcomes and latency are stored in `.consilium/reliability.json` (`models --reliability`). A composite GitHub Action runs a PR diff review and posts/updates one comment. ## Зачем нужен consilium

- **Разные модели — разные слепые зоны.** Одна модель пропускает то, что ловит другая; председатель делает конфликт явным, а не усредняет его.
- **Ноль стоимости по умолчанию.** Находит бесплатные модели с поддержкой tools в публичных каталогах, ранжирует их, проверяет, что они реально отвечают в вашем регионе, и прописывает в конфиг.
- **Работает с тем, что уже есть.** Авторизация, провайдеры и агенты — на стороне OpenCode CLI: никакого второго стека провайдеров и лишних ключей.
- **Один движок везде.** Терминал, MCP-сервер для любого харнесса, нативный плагин V2, API библиотеки.

`init --free`:

2. оставляет только бесплатные (`cost = 0`), активные чат-модели с tool calling и контекстом >= 32K;
3. ранжирует их и проверяет топ-кандидатов крошечным реальным запросом (если не указан `--no-verify`);
4. записывает победителей в `opencode.json` (агенты `arch`, `ux`, `ba`, `sec`, `consilium`) и `consilium.config.json`;
5. никогда не перезаписывает существующие модели агентов без `--force`.

## Работает на OpenCode V1 и V2

Поддерживаются обе ветки, формат конфигурации определяется автоматически.

| Что | OpenCode V1 | OpenCode V2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Агенты в `opencode.json` | `agent` + `prompt` | `agents` + `system` |
| MCP-серверы | `mcp.<name>` + `enabled` | `mcp.servers.<name>` + `disabled` |
| Команды | `command` + `subtask` | `commands` + `subagent` |
| Модель агента при `run --agent` | применяется из конфига | **игнорируется**, нужен `--model` |

- **Формат V1 — безопасный дефолт**: его читают обе версии, поэтому `init --free` пишет именно его. Конвертировать ничего не нужно.
- **Нативные V2-агенты** (`agents` + `system`) — только с `--native-v2` или если файл уже использует V2-ключи. MCP-сервер ставится отдельно: `consilium mcp --install`.
- **Модели всегда передаются через `--model`**, поэтому V2 не может молча откатиться на корневую модель.
- **Агенты читаются из обеих секций**, включая `.opencode/opencode.json(c)` и родительские каталоги; слияние идёт в том же порядке, что и в OpenCode (`.opencode` приоритетнее).
- `RATE_LIMITED` пережидает короткие лимиты (до 30 с) и быстро падает с задержкой повтора для длинных.
- `doctor` сообщает мажорную версию CLI, формат конфига, дубли `agent`/`agents`, мёртвые в V2 поля (`theme`, `autoupdate`) и плоские MCP-записи.

Регистрация MCP-сервера одной командой (формат выбирается по установленной версии OpenCode):

```bash
consilium mcp --install            # ./opencode.json
consilium mcp --install --global   # ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json
opencode mcp list                  # проверка
```

## Context pack (`--context auto`)

Эксперты обычно видят только задачу и diff. `--context auto` добавляет изменённые файлы, правила проекта (ближайший `AGENTS.md`), связанные тесты и недавние коммиты:

```bash
consilium --context auto --diff "Сделай ревью текущих изменений"
```

Приоритет и бюджет: правила → изменённые файлы → связанные тесты → коммиты; 48k символов всего, 12k на файл, 20 файлов. Бинарные, lock- и сгенерированные файлы пропускаются; каждая секция обёрнута в маркеры `<untrusted-*>`, чтобы текст репозитория не мог выдать себя за инструкции. `--context off` (по умолчанию) сохраняет прежнее поведение.

## OpenCode V1 / V2 兼容
两个分支都支持，配置形态自动识别。

| 项目 | OpenCode V1 | OpenCode V2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `opencode.json` Agent | `agent` + `prompt` | `agents` + `system` |
| MCP 服务器 | `mcp.<name>` + `enabled` | `mcp.servers.<name>` + `disabled` |
| 命令 | `command` + `subtask` | `commands` + `subagent` |
| `run --agent` 的模型 | 从配置应用 | **被忽略**，必须显式 `--model` |

默认写 V1 格式（两版都能读），原生 V2 仅在 `--native-v2` 或文件已用 V2 键时写入；模型始终以 `--model` 传递；Agent 从 `agent`/`agents`、`.opencode/opencode.json(c)` 及父目录读取。`RATE_LIMITED` 短时限（<= 30 秒）自动重试，长时限立即失败并给出延迟；`doctor` 报告 CLI 版本、配置格式与 V2 兼容问题。一键注册 MCP：`consilium mcp --install`（项目）、`consilium mcp --install --global`（全局），再用 `opencode mcp list` 验证。
## 上下文包（`--context auto`）
专家默认只看到任务和 diff。`--context auto` 会补充改动文件、最近的 `AGENTS.md`、相关测试和近期提交：

```bash
consilium --context auto --diff "Review the current changes"
```

优先级与预算：规则 → 改动文件 → 相关测试 → 提交；总计 48k 字符、单文件 12k、最多 20 个文件。二进制、锁文件和生成文件会跳过；每段都包在 `<untrusted-*>` 标记里，仓库文本无法冒充指令。`--context off`（默认）保持旧行为。
## 免费模型自动挑选
`consilium models`（前 20）、`--available`（仅可用提供商）、`--verify`（真实请求）、`--refresh`（忽略 12 小时缓存）、`--json`。来源：`models.dev`、OpenRouter 的 `:free` 变体和内置精选清单；缓存 `%TEMP%/lv24-opencode-consilium/models-cache.json`（或 `CONSILIUM_MODELS_CACHE`）。

当前推荐：`arch → opencode/flint-40b-free`、`ux → opencode/inkling-2-small-free`、`ba → opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free`、`sec → opencode/iceman-free`、`chair → opencode/beam-free`。`opencode-go` 的免费模型（`*-free` 等）也参与排序，但 `opencode-go/muse-spark-1.3-contributor` 这类付费模型不会被 `--free` 选中，需在 `experts[].model` 或 `chair.model` 指定。免费模型会轮换，`init --free` 复核目录与真实响应，`--refresh` 挑选替代者；排序（0–1.2）按上下文、tool calling、结构化输出、推理、新旧、输出上限、家族先验和付费同级“影子价格”加权。

调用结果记录在 `.consilium/reliability.json`（每个模型的成功、限流、超时、延迟）。`consilium models --reliability` 打印表格；模型累计至少 3 次尝试后，排序会接受可选的可信度加分。该文件仅本地保存，可安全删除。
## 本地与隐私模式
只在本机提供商上运行（Ollama、LM Studio、llama.cpp、vLLM）：

```bash
consilium models --local              # 排名目录中只保留本地模型
consilium models --probe-local        # Ollama / LM Studio 是否在运行？
consilium init --local                # 探测并写入 localOnly 配置
consilium init --local --dry-run      # 只预览模型分配，不写文件
consilium --local-only "Review the changes"
```

`init --local` 向 Ollama（`/api/tags`）和 LM Studio（`/v1/models`）查询模型列表，将模型轮流（round-robin）分配给 `arch`、`ux`、`ba`、`sec` 和主席，并写入含 `localOnly: true` 的 `consilium.config.json`（不加 `--force` 不覆盖现有文件）。支持 `--dry-run` 与 `--json`。

`--local-only` 是硬性保证：每位专家和主席都必须有明确的本地提供商模型，否则在启动前直接拒绝运行（退出码 2、MCP 工具错误或库错误）。缺少模型就是错误，不会隐式回退到云端。`doctor` 新增 `local-providers` 检查：当 `localOnly` 开启且没有任何本地提供商可达时，该检查失败。

# Consilium evaluation fixtures

This directory contains the self-contained corpus used by the deterministic
eval harness. The harness does **not** call an LLM judge: it runs a review
runner (the real council or an injected stub) and checks the returned
`Finding[]` against the phrases planted in each fixture.

The corpus currently has **22 fixtures**. It covers injection, authorization,
concurrency, reliability, SSRF and path traversal, data integrity,
pagination/caching and prompt injection.

## Layout

```text
eval/fixtures/<fixture-name>/
  task.md        # review request shown to the council
  changes.diff   # unified diff containing the planted bug
  expected.json  # mustFind / mustNotFind signatures
```

Fixture directories are loaded in lexicographic order, so a run is reproducible
across machines. `changes.diff` is optional for a task that needs no diff;
every fixture in the current corpus includes one.

## `expected.json`

```json
{
  "mustFind": [
    {
      "claimIncludes": ["sql injection", "untrusted order by"],
      "file": "src/db/users.ts",
      "minSeverity": "high"
    }
  ],
  "mustNotFind": [
    {
      "claimIncludes": "the default sort should remain created_at"
    }
  ]
}
```

- `mustFind` is required and must be a non-empty array. `mustNotFind` is
  optional and defaults to `[]`.
- Every entry must set at least one of `claimIncludes`, `file`, `category` or
  `minSeverity`; an empty filter would match every finding.
- `claimIncludes` may be a string or an array of alternatives. Each alternative
  is compared as a case-insensitive substring against `normalizeClaim(claim)`,
  so punctuation, quotes and repeated whitespace do not matter. This is a
  substring check, not a regex or an LLM judgement.
- `file` is the most robust signal: paths are lowercased, `\` is treated as
  `/`, a leading `./` is ignored, and a finding may use a longer root-relative
  path.
- `category` is an exact case-insensitive match. Models often use descriptive
  categories, so prefer `file` + `minSeverity` unless the category is known.
- `minSeverity` is optional. The finding severity must be at least this level
  (`critical` > `high` > `medium` > `low` > `info`).
- All filters in one entry are ANDed; one finding may satisfy several
  `mustFind` entries.
- `mustNotFind` entries use the same shape. A finding that matches one is
  counted as a false positive. Keep these claims clearly benign or out of scope
  so they measure noise rather than legitimate extra findings.

The 12 fixtures added for 1.11.0 deliberately rely on `claimIncludes` + `file` +
`minSeverity`. That keeps them language-neutral and robust to descriptive
category names; `category` remains supported by the loader and matcher.

## Running the eval

Prerequisites: Node.js 18+ and a configured `consilium.config.json` with
models that can review code. From a checkout:

```bash
npm install
npm run build
```

Run the bundled corpus with the real council:

```bash
# equivalent to the installed `consilium eval`
node bin/cli.js eval

# debate mode: one anonymized peer-review round before the chair
node bin/cli.js eval --rounds 2

# run every fixture twice (rounds=1 and rounds=2) and print the delta table
node bin/cli.js eval --compare-rounds

# machine-readable summary
node bin/cli.js eval --json

# machine-readable single-vs-debate comparison
node bin/cli.js eval --compare-rounds --json
```

When the package is installed, replace `node bin/cli.js` with `consilium`:

```bash
consilium eval
consilium eval --rounds 2
consilium eval --compare-rounds
consilium eval --json
```

Useful options:

| Option | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `--fixtures <dir>` | Use another fixture directory (default `eval/fixtures`) |
| `--rounds <1\|2>` | Number of debate rounds for every fixture (default `1`) |
| `--compare-rounds` | Run the same fixtures with one and two rounds; mutually exclusive with `--rounds` |
| `--json` | Print the summary or comparison as JSON instead of markdown |
| `--fail-under <pct>` | Exit `3` when the catch rate is below the percentage (debate catch rate in compare mode) |
| `--max-cost <usd>` | Stop the suite when the accumulated cost reaches the budget (both runs in compare mode) |

`--compare-rounds` prints a `single` / `debate` / `delta` table and also lists
errors for each run. A failed fixture runner still counts as a miss and does
not abort the suite. Exit code `3` is the eval policy gate; usage errors are
`2`.

## Metrics

For each fixture the matcher reports:

- `caught` — `mustFind` entries with at least one matching finding.
- `missed` — `mustFind` entries with no match.
- `falsePositives` — `mustNotFind` entries that a finding matched.
- `catchRate` — `caught / (caught + missed)`; `0` when there is nothing to find.
- `falsePositiveRate` — `falsePositives / (caught + falsePositives)`; `0` when the
  denominator is empty.

The suite summary aggregates those counts, reports the p50 latency (the mean of
the two middle values for an even number of fixtures), totals runner cost, and
lists runner errors. A fixture whose runner throws still counts as a miss.

## Results

No model benchmark numbers are stored in this directory. Catch rate, latency
and cost depend on the exact model set, provider availability and date, so any
published table must come from a real run rather than an estimate.

To produce a result set, run:

```bash
npm run build
node bin/cli.js eval --json > eval-single.json
node bin/cli.js eval --rounds 2 --json > eval-debate.json
node bin/cli.js eval --compare-rounds --json > eval-compare.json
```

Record the date, fixture count, configured experts and model ids next to the
JSON output. Re-run on the target machine instead of reusing another machine's
numbers.

## Generating the report

[`scripts/eval-report.mjs`](../scripts/eval-report.mjs) turns those JSON files
into the markdown report. It reads `eval/fixtures` for the coverage table and
refuses to write when a required field is missing, so it cannot silently publish
placeholder numbers.

```bash
# Full single-vs-debate report; writes docs/eval-results.md by default.
node scripts/eval-report.mjs --compare eval-compare.json

# Single-run report.
node scripts/eval-report.mjs --single eval-single.json

# Validate the inputs and print a summary without writing anything.
node scripts/eval-report.mjs --check --compare eval-compare.json

# Equivalent npm script (arguments after -- are passed through).
npm run eval:report -- --compare eval-compare.json
```

Useful options: `--out <file>` (default `docs/eval-results.md`),
`--date <YYYY-MM-DD>`, `--commit <sha>`, `--version <version>` and
`--fixtures <dir>` (default `eval/fixtures`). The generated file contains the
exact commands, the aggregate single/debate/delta table, per-fixture metrics,
missed findings, false positives, errors and the on-disk fixture count (22 in
the current corpus).

The JSON does not contain model or provider ids, so keep the configured expert
set next to the report. Do not compare runs with different fixtures or models.
The generator lives in the repository checkout; `scripts/` is not part of the
published npm package, so run it from a clone.

## Adding a fixture

1. Create a directory named `<number>-<short-category>` under `eval/fixtures/`.
2. Write a short `task.md` that gives the reviewer enough context, including
   the security or correctness property that must hold.
3. Add a small unified diff (roughly 5–15 changed lines) with exactly one
   planted bug. Keep unrelated code boring so a finding points at the bug.
4. Add `expected.json` with a distinctive `claimIncludes` phrase (or a few
   alternatives), the affected `file` and a realistic `minSeverity`. Add one
   benign `mustNotFind` phrase for noise when useful.
5. Update the corpus table below and the fixture count in
   `test/eval.test.mjs` when the total changes.

# lv24-opencode-consilium

> A council of AI experts for OpenCode: four expert agents (`arch`, `ux`, `ba`, `sec`) answer in parallel on different models, then a chair model synthesizes one plan. CLI, MCP server, native OpenCode V2 plugin and library API. Free-model bootstrap included.

Version: 1.12.1 · License: MIT · Node: >= 18 · Runtime dependencies: none

## Install

- `npm install -g lv24-opencode-consilium`
- `npx -y lv24-opencode-consilium --help`
- `pip install lv24-opencode-consilium` — thin Python launcher that delegates to the npm CLI via `npx` (still needs Node.js >= 18 and OpenCode; npm is canonical).
- Container: `docker pull ghcr.io/levapveeskela/lv24-opencode-consilium:1.12.1`
- Requires the OpenCode CLI (`npm install -g opencode-ai`), authenticated; V1 or V2.

## Commands

- `consilium doctor` — environment, config, agents and model diagnostics.
- `consilium init --free [--dry-run] [--force] [--no-verify] [--native-v2]` — discover, rank, probe and write free models.
- `consilium models [--available] [--verify] [--limit N] [--refresh] [--json]` — ranked free models.
- `consilium [options] "<task>"` — run the council; `-f json` prints one JSON document on stdout.
- `consilium mcp [--install] [--global]` — stdio MCP server or config registration.
- `consilium watch [--debounce <ms>] [task]` — rerun on file changes.
- `consilium hooks install|uninstall` — managed git pre-commit review hook.
- `consilium --replay <id>` / `consilium --diff-runs <a> <b>` — rerun or compare saved artifacts.
- `consilium baseline accept|prune` — manage `.consilium/baseline.json`.
- `consilium eval [--fixtures <dir>] [--json] [--fail-under <pct>] [--max-cost <usd>]` — deterministic planted-bug suite.
- `consilium history [--limit N] [--json]` / `consilium stats [--json] [--html <file>]` — recent runs, success rate, p50/p95, cost, per-model errors.
- `consilium presets [--json]` — built-in and custom presets.
- `--deadline <ms>` — cap the expert phase; partial synthesis with `metadata.deadline`.
- `--local-only` — require explicit local models; `models --local` / `--probe-local`.
- `consilium init --local [--dry-run] [--force]` — probe Ollama/LM Studio and write a `localOnly` config.
- `--rounds <1|2>` — second anonymized peer-review round; `metadata.debate`.
- `consilium audit --since <ref> [--dry-run] [--fail-on <severity>]` — review `<ref>...HEAD` end-to-end.
- `--read-only` — experts/chair may only read/glob/grep; write/edit/shell/webfetch/subagent/MCP tools denied. `audit` and the GitHub Action default to it; `--allow-write` opts out.
- `--isolate` — each agent runs in a Consilium-managed git worktree under `.consilium/worktrees`; requires git, includes tracked changes, removes the worktree after the call.
- `--report jira|linear --report-file ticket.jira|ticket.md` — Jira wiki / Linear Markdown ticket body.
- `--report sarif --report-file report.sarif` — SARIF 2.1.0 for code scanning (findings required).
- `consilium sarif [--run <id|latest>] [--output <file>]` — export SARIF from saved artifacts without re-running.
- `consilium eval --compare-rounds` / `--rounds 2` — compare single-pass vs debate catch/FP/latency/cost.
- Scheduling recipes: docs/scheduling.md (cron, Task Scheduler, launchd, GitHub Actions).
- `--context <off|auto>` — add changed files, rules, tests and commits to the task.
- `consilium models --reliability` — per-model success/latency table.

## Findings and gate

- `--findings` — experts/chair return a fenced JSON block with `findings[]` and `rejected[]`.
- `metadata.findings` = `{ items, counts, rejected, parseErrors }`; findings are deduped by fingerprint (plus fuzzy paraphrases), max severity, `contested` when rejected.
- `--fail-on <severity>` — exit `3` when new findings reach the threshold.
- Baseline: `.consilium/baseline.json` via `consilium baseline accept|prune`; accepted fingerprints are ignored by the gate.

## Safety

- `--read-only` writes a temporary `.opencode/opencode.json` layer with V2 `agents.<name>.permissions` and V1 `agent.<name>.tools`, holds `.consilium/read-only.lock`, backs up an existing layer and restores it on success/error/cancel/exit. Invalid JSON, an existing `.opencode/opencode.jsonc` or symlinked layer fails closed.
- `metadata.safety = { readOnly, isolate }` records the effective policy in results/artifacts.
- `--isolate` creates a managed git worktree per agent under `.consilium/worktrees`, includes tracked uncommitted changes, does not copy untracked files, applies the read-only overlay inside each worktree, and removes it after the call; stale cleanup handles crashed runs.

## Machine contract

- stdout: data only. stderr: progress and logs.
- JSON mode: `consilium -f json "<task>"` → result + `metadata` (models, usage, cost, consensus, artifacts, safety, errorCode).
- Models JSON: `consilium models --json`.
- Exit codes: `0` success, `1` run failed, `2` usage error, `3` policy/eval gate failed.
- Typed errors: `RATE_LIMITED`, `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE`, `EMPTY_RESPONSE`, `AGENT_NOT_FOUND`, `COST_LIMIT`, `TIMEOUT`.
- Cost cap: `--max-cost <usd>`; when exceeded before the chair, a partial result with `errorCode: COST_LIMIT` is returned.
- Sessions: `--session <id>`; each agent gets `ses_<base>-<agent>`, the chair continues the base session.
- State: files under `.consilium/runs/<id>/` (`run.json`, `report.md`, `experts/<agent>.md`); no daemon, no database.
- Deadline: `--deadline <ms>` → `metadata.deadline = { limitMs, hit, completed, missing }`; zero completed experts → `errorCode: DEADLINE`.
- Privacy: `--local-only` requires an explicit local provider (`ollama`, `lmstudio`, `llamacpp`, `vllm`) for every agent; otherwise the run is rejected before spawning.
- Debate: `--rounds 2` → `metadata.debate = { rounds, participants, changed }`; round 2 doubles model calls and is skipped on low expert count, deadline or cost limit.

- Command: `npx -y lv24-opencode-consilium mcp` (stdio JSON-RPC 2.0).

# Architecture

`lv24-opencode-consilium` is a TypeScript ESM package (`module`/`moduleResolution`
set to `NodeNext`), so every relative import ends in `.js`. Source lives in
`src/`; compiled output in `dist/`; tests are plain `.mjs` files under `test/`
and import from `dist/`.

## Layer map

| Layer | Location | Responsibility |
| --- | --- | --- |
| shared | `src/shared/` | Dependency-free primitives used by every layer: JSON record checks (`record.ts`), error text extraction (`errors.ts`), and atomic file writing (`fs.ts`). No business logic. |
| domain | `src/domain/` | Entities, config types, defaults, and pure policies: council (`presets`, `variants`, `consensus`, `fallback`, `smart-experts`, `findings`, `prompts`, `sessions`), models (`catalog`, `ranking`, `model-ref`), artifacts (`artifacts/*`, `replay`, `report`, `findings-summary`, `ticket`, `baseline`), eval (`types`, `matcher`). |
| application | `src/application/` | Use cases and orchestration: `Consilium` (`consilium.ts`), the run pipeline (`run.ts`), findings collection (`findings.ts`), the eval suite (`eval.ts`), prompt/usage helpers (`helpers.ts`), model verification (`models/verify.ts`) and diagnostics (`diagnostics/`: `checks`, `doctor`, `report`). It coordinates domain policies and infrastructure adapters. |
| infrastructure | `src/infrastructure/` | Adapters to the outside world: config loading/merging/validation (`config/`), OpenCode CLI process control (`opencode/`, including the temporary read-only overlay and managed isolated worktrees), artifact storage (`artifacts/store.ts`), free-model catalog fetching/cache and reliability memory (`models/`), context pack (`context.ts`), git (`git.ts`), and filesystem watching (`watch.ts`). |
| interfaces | `src/interfaces/` | Delivery mechanisms: CLI (`cli/`), MCP stdio server (`mcp/`), and the OpenCode plugin (`plugin/`). They parse input, call application services, and format output. |

The domain layer is I/O-free: it has no `node:fs`/`node:net`/`fetch` calls and no
imports from `infrastructure/`, `application/` or `interfaces/`. File, process and
network access lives in `infrastructure/` and is called from `application/` or
`interfaces/`.

## Dependency direction

```
interfaces ──> application ──> domain
      │              │
      └──────────────┴──────> infrastructure ──> domain
every layer ──> shared
```

- `shared` imports nothing from the other layers.
- `domain` imports only `shared`.
- `application` may import `domain` and `infrastructure` (it loads config and
  starts OpenCode runs), never `interfaces`.
- `infrastructure` may import `domain` types/helpers, never `application` or
  `interfaces`.
- `interfaces` may import `application`, `domain`, and `infrastructure`. One
  entry-point composition is intentional: `cli/main.ts` imports
  `interfaces/mcp/mcp.ts` to serve the `mcp` command.
- `interfaces/mcp/handlers/shared.ts` is a slice-local helper, not part of the
  `src/shared/` kernel.
- Never import another slice's internals; use its barrel. Avoid cycles: shared
  code moves down a layer, not sideways.

## Barrels and compatibility shims

- Slice barrels are the public API of their slice:
  `interfaces/cli/index.ts`, `interfaces/mcp/index.ts`,
  `interfaces/plugin/index.ts`, `infrastructure/config/index.ts`,
  `infrastructure/opencode/index.ts`, `domain/council/index.ts`,
  `domain/models/index.ts`, `domain/artifacts/index.ts`, and
  `application/diagnostics/index.ts`. Internal code may deep-import modules
  inside its own layer.
- There are no layer-level `index.ts` files: `src/domain/index.ts`,
  `src/infrastructure/index.ts`, `src/application/index.ts` and
  `src/shared/index.ts` do not exist.
- `interfaces/cli/cli.ts` is the CLI slice's public entry and exports exactly
  `parseArgs` and `main`. `interfaces/mcp/mcp.ts` is the MCP slice entry.
- The files directly under `src/` are compatibility shims. They preserve the
  historical `dist/` module paths used by the package `exports` map and by the
  `.mjs` tests that import from `dist/`: each one re-exports its implementation,
  e.g. `src/mcp.ts` → `./interfaces/mcp/mcp.js`, `src/config.ts` →
  `./infrastructure/config/config.js`, `src/agents.ts` →
  `./infrastructure/opencode/agents.js`, `src/doctor.ts` →
  `./application/diagnostics/doctor.js`, `src/verify.ts` →
  `./application/models/verify.js`. `src/git.ts` and `src/types.ts` are kept for
  tests/internal compatibility even though they are not package exports. Add new
  public subpaths the same way rather than moving implementations back to `src/`.
- `src/index.ts` is the public library API and exports `application/consilium.js`.
- `src/cli.ts` is both a shim and the executable compatibility entry: it
  re-exports `interfaces/cli/cli.js` and auto-runs `main()` only when
  `process.argv[1]` resolves to its own module file. `bin/cli.js` imports it and
  calls `main` explicitly, so the guard stays false there.

## Adding a CLI command

1. Extend the `command` union in `CLIOptions` (`domain/types.ts`) and add the
   name to `COMMANDS` in `interfaces/cli/args.ts`.
2. Parse the command's flags in `parseArgs` (`interfaces/cli/args.ts`) into
   `CLIOptions`; throw `UsageError` for invalid input.
3. Create `interfaces/cli/commands/<name>.ts` exporting
   `command<Name>(options: CLIOptions): Promise<number>`; return the exit code.
4. Add the `case '<name>'` to the switch in `interfaces/cli/main.ts`.
5. Document flags in `interfaces/cli/help.ts`; reuse printers from
   `interfaces/cli/output.ts`.
6. Add coverage in `test/cli.test.mjs` (tests run against `dist/`).

## Adding an MCP tool

1. Append an `McpToolDef` to `MCP_TOOLS` in `interfaces/mcp/tools.ts`
   (`MCP_TOOL_NAMES` and `getMcpTools()` derive from it automatically).
2. Implement the handler in `interfaces/mcp/handlers/<name>.ts`, returning
   `McpToolResult` from `handlers/shared.js`; validate input with
   `interfaces/mcp/validation.ts` helpers and call application services.
3. Route it in the `executeTool` switch in `handlers/dispatch.ts` and export it
   from `handlers/index.ts` when it is part of the slice API.
4. Wrap failures with `toolError(...)`; `executeTool` already catches exceptions.
5. Add coverage in `test/mcp.test.mjs`.

## Adding a config key

1. Add the field to `ConsiliumConfig` in `domain/types.ts` (and to `CLIOptions`
   if a flag overrides it).
2. Set its default in `DEFAULT_CONFIG` (`domain/defaults.ts`).
3. Handle it in `infrastructure/config/load.ts`: `cloneConfig` and
   `mergeWithDefaults` for nested objects/arrays, plus a warning in
   `validateConfig` when the value is out of range.
4. For a CLI flag, parse it in `interfaces/cli/args.ts`, apply it in
   `interfaces/cli/overrides.ts`, and document it in `help.ts`. Work on the
   already-cloned config; never mutate `DEFAULT_CONFIG`.
5. Update `consilium.config.example.json`, `schema/config.schema.json`, and
   `generateExampleConfig()` in `infrastructure/config/generate.ts`.
6. Read the value from `application/` code (usually `Consilium`), not from
   interface code, so every entry point gets the same behavior.

# Consilium GitHub Action for pull request reviews

A composite GitHub Action that runs the Consilium council on a pull request
diff, posts or updates **one** sticky review comment, and can fail the job when
new findings reach a severity threshold.

It is designed to be zero-spend:

- The action runs on the caller's GitHub Actions runner.
- It installs the public npm package and, if needed, the OpenCode CLI.
- It talks only to the GitHub API and the model provider you already use.
- There is no hosted Consilium app, no GitHub App installation, and no paid
  Consilium service.

You still pay for GitHub Actions minutes according to your plan, and model
providers may apply quotas or charges. See [Cost and quotas](#cost-and-quotas).

## Files

| Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `.github/actions/consilium/action.yml` | Composite action: setup, install, run, comment, gate |
| `.github/actions/consilium/comment.mjs` | Node 20 ESM script that creates or updates the PR comment |
| `examples/consilium-review.yml` | Example caller workflow. **Not enabled by default** |

The example deliberately lives under `examples/`. GitHub Actions only runs
workflows under `.github/workflows/`, so copying the repository does not start
any review or spend any quota.

## Requirements

- A GitHub Actions runner with `bash` (`ubuntu-latest` is recommended).
- Outbound network access to npm, the GitHub API, and your model provider.
- `actions/checkout` with `fetch-depth: 0`, so the base branch is available for
  `git diff`.
- An authenticated OpenCode CLI and at least one model configuration.
  - The action installs `opencode-ai` when `opencode` is not on `PATH`, but it
    does not authenticate it for you.
  - Provide credentials through repository or environment secrets, for example
    `OPENCODE_API_KEY` or `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` (Settings -> Secrets and
    variables -> Actions), or configure the provider key your OpenCode setup
    expects. A self-hosted runner can also use its existing OpenCode login.
  - For predictable reviews, commit a `consilium.config.json` with the models
    and experts you want. Generate it locally with
    `consilium init --free` (or `npx -y lv24-opencode-consilium init --free`)
    and review the generated files before committing them. The action does not
    run `init` automatically because it writes project files and probes models.
- `pull-requests: write` for the comment. See [Permissions](#permissions).
- `security-events: write` when SARIF upload is enabled (the default), and code
  scanning must be enabled for the repository. See
  [SARIF and code scanning](#sarif-and-code-scanning).

## Installation

### Option A: use the action from this repository

Pin the action to a commit SHA (recommended) or a release tag:

```yaml
- name: Run Consilium
  uses: LevapVeeskela/lv24-opencode-consilium/.github/actions/consilium@<full-commit-sha>
  with:
    version: '1.12.1'
  env:
    OPENCODE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENCODE_API_KEY }}
```

Replace `<full-commit-sha>` with the commit you reviewed. If the repository is
private, the caller workflow must have access to it.

### Option B: vendor the action

Copy `.github/actions/consilium/` into the caller repository and use a local
path. This is what `examples/consilium-review.yml` does:

```yaml
- name: Run Consilium
  uses: ./.github/actions/consilium
  with:
    fail-on: high
  env:
    OPENCODE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENCODE_API_KEY }}
```

For a local action, check out the repository before the `uses` step.

### Minimal workflow

```yaml
name: Consilium PR review

on:
  pull_request:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
  security-events: write

jobs:
  review:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - uses: ./.github/actions/consilium
        with:
          fail-on: high
          comment: 'true'
        env:
          OPENCODE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENCODE_API_KEY }}
```

## Inputs and outputs

| Input | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `task` | Review instructions | Task passed to Consilium. Defaults to a focused correctness/security/regression review. |
| `base` | empty | Git ref to diff against. Empty means `origin/<github.base_ref>`. The action validates the ref before running. |
| `fail-on` | `none` | Gate threshold: `critical`, `high`, `medium`, `low`, `info`, or `none`. |
| `comment` | `true` | Post or update the sticky comment. `false` still applies the gate. |
| `github-token` | `${{ github.token }}` | Token for the comment API. Needs `pull-requests: write`. |
| `node-version` | `20` | Node.js version used by the action. |
| `max-cost` | empty | Optional soft cost cap in USD, passed to `--max-cost`. |
| `read-only` | `true` | Pass `--read-only`: experts may only read/glob/grep; write/edit/shell/subagent/MCP tools are denied. Set to `false` to pass `--allow-write`. |
| `version` | `latest` | npm version of `lv24-opencode-consilium` to install. Pin an exact version for reproducibility. |
| `sarif` | `true` | Export findings as SARIF 2.1.0 and upload them to GitHub code scanning. Requires `security-events: write` and code scanning enabled for the repository. Set to `false` to skip both SARIF steps. |
| `sarif-file` | `consilium.sarif` | Path to the generated SARIF file, relative to the workspace or absolute. |
| `category` | `consilium` | Category passed to `github/codeql-action/upload-sarif`, so several SARIF reports can coexist in one repository. |

Outputs:

| Output | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `exit-code` | Consilium CLI exit code (`0`, `1`, `2`, or `3`). |
| `report-file` | Absolute path to `consilium-review.md` in the workspace. |

When `fail-on` is not `none` or `sarif` is `true`, the action adds
`--findings` automatically. The CLI requires structured findings for the gate
and for a non-empty SARIF report; without this, the gate would exit `2` before
producing a report.

## Permissions

The workflow needs at least:

```yaml
permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
  security-events: write
```

`contents: read` lets `actions/checkout` fetch the repository and lets the
action compute the diff. `pull-requests: write` allows listing issue comments
on the PR and creating or updating the Consilium comment. `security-events:
write` is required only for SARIF uploads (the default `sarif: true`); remove it
when `sarif: false`.

Set permissions at the workflow or job level. If your organization sets a
restricted default `GITHUB_TOKEN` policy, grant `pull-requests: write` and
`security-events: write` in the workflow or repository settings. The action does
not need `contents: write`, `issues: write`, `actions: write`, or a personal
access token.

The `github-token` input defaults to `${{ github.token }}`. Prefer that scoped
token to a long-lived PAT. A PAT is only useful if your organization's policy
prevents the workflow token from commenting, and it increases the blast radius
if leaked.

## Comment behavior

Consilium writes a GitHub-ready report with `--report pr --report-file
consilium-review.md`. The report ends with the hidden marker:

```html
<!-- consilium:report -->
```

`comment.mjs`:

1. Reads `GITHUB_EVENT_PATH` and takes `pull_request.number`.
2. Lists the PR's issue comments and looks for the marker.
3. `PATCH`es the existing comment, or `POST`s a new one.
4. Caps the body at about 60,000 characters. The marker and a truncation note
   are preserved, so the next run still finds and updates the same comment.
5. Treats `403` and `404` as warnings and exits `0`. This covers missing
   `pull-requests: write`, read-only fork PR tokens, deleted PRs, and rate
   limits. Other comment/API/network failures are also warnings so they cannot
   hide the review gate.
6. Never logs `GITHUB_TOKEN`.

The script posts only on pull request events. If the event has no
`pull_request.number`, it warns and exits `0`.

Set `comment: false` to run the review and enforce the gate without touching the
PR. The action skips the script when `comment` is not `true` or when
`github-token` is empty, and the gate still runs.

Comment failures do not turn a passing review into a failing job, and they do
not replace exit code `3`. If the comment matters for branch protection, monitor
the workflow warnings or add a separate check for the comment step's outcome.

## Read-only reviews

The action enables `--read-only` by default. The review can read files, glob and
grep, but cannot write, edit, patch, run a shell, fetch the web, launch
subagents or call MCP tools. This is enforced with a temporary project
`.opencode/opencode.json` layer that is restored after the run; an existing
`.opencode/opencode.jsonc` fails closed.

Set `read-only: false` to pass `--allow-write` when a workflow intentionally
lets the council modify the workspace. The effective policy is recorded in
`metadata.safety` and in the run artifacts.

## SARIF and code scanning

The review run always writes artifacts with `--artifacts`, so
`.consilium/runs/<id>/run.json` exists. When `sarif` is `true` (the default), the
action also adds `--findings` so `run.json` contains `metadata.findings`.

After the review, the action:

1. Runs `consilium sarif --run latest --output consilium.sarif` (or the path in
   `sarif-file`). This step uses `continue-on-error: true`.
2. Uploads the file with `github/codeql-action/upload-sarif`, passing
   `sarif_file` and `category`. This step also uses `continue-on-error: true`.

Both SARIF steps are independent of the gate. A missing permission, a disabled
code scanning setup, or an upload failure produces a warning or a failed step,
but it does not replace exit code `3` and does not turn a passing review into a
failing job. The comment and gate steps still run.

Requirements for SARIF upload:

- `security-events: write` on the workflow or job.
- Code scanning must be enabled for the repository. Public repositories can use
  code scanning directly; private repositories may require GitHub Advanced
  Security depending on your plan. If code scanning is unavailable, set
  `sarif: false` and keep the review comment and gate.
- On fork pull requests the token is read-only, so uploads fail; that is
  expected and does not affect the gate.

Use a Consilium package version that includes the `consilium sarif` command. If
the example pins an older version, either upgrade it or set `sarif: false`.

The SARIF file contains every finding from the run. Findings accepted in
`.consilium/baseline.json` still appear there; the baseline only changes the
gate result. Use `consilium sarif` locally to inspect the same document:

```bash
consilium sarif --run latest --output consilium.sarif
```

## Fork pull request caveat

Pull requests from forks do **not** receive repository secrets, and GitHub gives
their workflow a read-only `GITHUB_TOKEN`. That means:

- `OPENCODE_API_KEY`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, and other model credentials are
  unavailable, so Consilium usually cannot run.
- The comment API returns `403` (or `404` in some configurations). The script
  warns and exits `0`; the action still applies the review gate.
- The example workflow skips fork PRs with:

  ```yaml
  if: >-
    github.event.pull_request.draft == false &&
    github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
  ```

Do not switch to `pull_request_target` just to obtain secrets while checking out
and running untrusted pull request code. That combination is a well-known
secret-exfiltration risk. If you need fork reviews, use a separately designed
trusted workflow, require maintainer approval before exposing credentials, or
run on a self-hosted runner with an explicit security boundary. Consilium
reviews a diff and does not execute pull request code, but the workflow, project
config, and installed dependencies are still part of your trust boundary.

A maintainer can also run the review manually from a trusted branch after
reviewing the diff.

## Cost and quotas

The action itself is free software and uses no paid Consilium backend. The main
costs are:

- **GitHub Actions minutes.** Public repositories get free minutes; private
  repositories consume the plan's included minutes. A review can take several
  minutes because it waits for multiple models.
- **Model provider usage.** Free models may be rate-limited or time out. If you
  configure paid models, their provider bills you directly.
- **npm downloads.** The action installs the Consilium package and, when
  missing, the OpenCode CLI. This is ordinary npm traffic, not a paid service.

`max-cost` is a **soft** cap. Consilium tracks reported spend and skips the chair
when the expert phase exceeds the limit, returning a partial result. It cannot
stop a provider from charging more if the provider does not report cost; in that
case Consilium warns that the limit cannot be verified. Treat it as a guardrail,
not a hard budget. Start with free models and a small `max-cost` while testing.

## Gate behavior and exit code 3

Exit codes come from the Consilium CLI:

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | Review completed and the gate passed. |
| `1` | The review run failed. |
| `2` | Usage error, invalid input, or missing base ref. |
| `3` | Policy gate failed: new findings at or above `fail-on` remain. |

The gate compares findings with `.consilium/baseline.json`. Fingerprints in the
baseline are accepted and ignored. To accept known findings, run locally:

```bash
consilium baseline accept latest
```

Commit `.consilium/baseline.json` if the whole team should share the accepted
set. Otherwise every PR starts with an empty baseline.

The action order is deliberate:

1. Run Consilium and capture its exit code with `set +e`.
2. Write `consilium-review.md`.
3. Export `consilium.sarif` and upload it when `sarif` is `true`.
4. Post or update the comment.
5. Re-exit with the captured code.

A failing gate therefore never skips the comment or the SARIF upload. A failing
comment or SARIF upload never replaces the gate code. If `comment: false` is
set, the review, report, SARIF, and gate steps still run.

`fail-on` levels, from most to least severe: `critical`, `high`, `medium`, `low`,
`info`. The default `none` disables the gate and keeps the job green. To make the
gate blocking in branch protection, require the workflow check and keep the
threshold meaningful for your repository.

## Pinning versions

Three things can move independently:

1. **The action ref.** Pin `uses:` to a full commit SHA (or a reviewed release
   tag) instead of `@main`.
2. **The npm package.** Pass an exact `version`, for example `1.12.1`, instead
   of the default `latest`.
3. **The OpenCode CLI.** The action installs `opencode-ai@latest` only when
   `opencode` is not already on `PATH`. To pin it, install a specific version in
   an earlier step:

   ```yaml
   - name: Pin OpenCode CLI
     run: npm install --global opencode-ai@1.19.5

   - name: Run Consilium
     uses: ./.github/actions/consilium
     with:
       version: '1.12.1'
   ```

   Also pin `actions/checkout` to a commit SHA in production workflows.

Example remote pin:

```yaml
- uses: LevapVeeskela/lv24-opencode-consilium/.github/actions/consilium@<full-commit-sha>
  with:
    version: '1.12.1'
    fail-on: high
```

Avoid `@main` and `version: latest` for required checks. They make a review
change without a commit in your repository.

## Troubleshooting

### `Base ref 'origin/...' was not found`

The most common cause is a shallow checkout. Set `fetch-depth: 0` on
`actions/checkout`. Make sure the base branch is fetched (a full checkout does
this) or pass it explicitly:

```yaml
with:
  base: origin/develop
```

If the workflow does not run on a `pull_request` event, `github.base_ref` is
empty. Pass `base` explicitly or restrict the action to pull request events.
The action validates `${base}^{commit}` before running and exits `2` with a
clear error if it cannot resolve the ref.

### The comment is missing, or HTTP 403/404

Check:

- The workflow has `pull-requests: write`.
- The PR is not from a fork. Fork PRs use a read-only token and receive no
  secrets.
- Your organization has not restricted `GITHUB_TOKEN` to read-only.
- The run did not hit GitHub API rate limits.
- `comment` is `true` and `github-token` is non-empty.
- `consilium-review.md` exists and contains the report. A missing report is
  reported as a warning, and the gate still runs.

The action logs the HTTP status and a warning but does not fail the job for
comment problems. Inspect the "Post or update the Consilium review comment"
step.

### The comment is not updated

The report must contain `<!-- consilium:report -->`. The action uses
`--report pr`, which writes the marker. If the report is longer than about
60,000 characters, the script truncates it but keeps the marker and a note.
If multiple comments contain the marker, the script updates the first one it
finds.

### `OpenCode CLI` or model errors

The action installs the CLI if it is missing, but it cannot supply credentials
or a model catalog. Check:

- The secret is passed to the action's `env` (for example
  `OPENCODE_API_KEY`).
- A `consilium.config.json` exists with enabled experts and models, or OpenCode
  has a usable default model.
- The provider is reachable from the runner and the model is available in your
  region.
- Run `consilium doctor` locally with the same config.

### The gate fails unexpectedly

Reproduce the review locally with the same command:

```bash
consilium --diff --base origin/main --report pr \
  --report-file consilium-review.md --fail-on high \
  --findings -s "Review this pull request"
```

Check `.consilium/baseline.json` and whether the finding is new. Remember that
`--fail-on` gates only on findings not present in the baseline. Use
`fail-on: none` if you want a comment-only review.

### `max-cost` did not stop the run

The provider may not report cost. Consilium can only enforce the cap from
reported usage; it warns when telemetry is missing. Switch to a provider that
reports cost or use free models with external quota monitoring.

### The action fails during install

Check npm registry access on the runner, Node compatibility, and global install
permissions on self-hosted runners. On a self-hosted runner, preinstall pinned
`lv24-opencode-consilium` and `opencode-ai` versions to avoid network and
permission surprises.

## Security notes

- The token is passed only to `comment.mjs` through `GITHUB_TOKEN`. The script
  never prints it and never writes it to the report.
- Use the default scoped `GITHUB_TOKEN` with `contents: read` and
  `pull-requests: write`; avoid broad PATs.
- Review model output before treating it as authoritative. The report is
  posted as markdown and may contain arbitrary text produced from the diff.
- Do not run untrusted pull request code with repository secrets. The
  `pull_request` trigger plus the example's fork guard avoids that pattern.
- Consilium ignores process/path keys from an untrusted project config unless
  the config is explicitly trusted; keep `autoApprove` off.
- No secrets belong in `.github/actions/consilium/`, `examples/`, or this
  document. Use repository or environment secrets in the caller workflow.

# PyPI publishing

`lv24-opencode-consilium` is published on PyPI as a small Python wrapper around
the canonical npm CLI. `pip install lv24-opencode-consilium` installs the
`consilium` CLI and `consilium-mcp` MCP server console scripts, which delegate
to the npm package through `npx`.
The council engine, models, prompts, MCP server and plugin live in the npm
package. **npm remains the canonical distribution**: PyPI mirrors the same
version and is not a second source of features.

## Requirements

- Python 3.9+ (`requires-python` in `python/pyproject.toml`); the publish
  workflow uses Python 3.12.
- Node.js >= 18, including npm and npx.
- An authenticated OpenCode CLI: `npm install -g opencode-ai`.
- Network access on first run (or a warm npm cache), because `npx` may download
  the npm package. The wrapper does not bundle Node.js or OpenCode.

## One-time setup (Trusted Publishing)

No API token or repository secret is used: PyPI trusts GitHub's OIDC identity.

1. Create a PyPI account at <https://pypi.org/account/register/> and enable
   two-factor authentication; PyPI requires 2FA for publishing.
2. Open <https://pypi.org/manage/account/publishing/> and add a **pending
   trusted publisher**. The project does not exist yet, which is expected.

   | Field | Value |
   | --- | --- |
   | PyPI project name | `lv24-opencode-consilium` |
   | Owner | `LevapVeeskela` |
   | Repository name | `lv24-opencode-consilium` |
   | Workflow name | `pypi-publish.yml` |
   | Environment name | blank (or `pypi`, see below) |

3. Save. The first successful publish creates the project and converts the
   pending publisher into a normal trusted publisher. Do not create the project
   manually first, and do not add an API token.

The committed workflow has no `environment:`, so leave the PyPI environment
blank. For a GitHub environment named `pypi`, add `environment: pypi` to the
`publish` job and enter `pypi` on PyPI; both values must match exactly.

## Release flow

Publishing a GitHub release for tag `vX.Y.Z` triggers both npm-publish and
pypi-publish. Bump every version copy before tagging: `package.json` (and the
root fields in `package-lock.json`), `python/pyproject.toml`,
`python/src/lv24_opencode_consilium/__init__.py` (`__version__`), the config
and MCP protocol defaults, `llms.txt`, the container workflow and the README
tags. The PyPI workflow fails fast if the tag, `package.json`,
`python/pyproject.toml` or `__version__` differ; `npm test` runs
`test/version-consistency.test.mjs`, which checks the rest.

1. Bump the version files and run the usual checks (`npm test`,
   `python -m build` in `python/`).
2. Commit, tag (`git tag vX.Y.Z`), push, and publish a GitHub release.
3. Watch the `pypi-publish` run in Actions.

Manual fallback, for example when a release tag predates the workflow:

```bash
gh workflow run pypi-publish.yml -f version=1.12.1
```

The input may include or omit the leading `v`. Existing versions are detected
through the public JSON API and skipped, so re-running is safe. PyPI never
allows re-uploading a filename; bump the version to replace a bad release.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| `invalid-publisher` or `Trusted publishing failed` | The owner, repository, workflow filename or environment does not match the pending publisher. Use `LevapVeeskela`, `lv24-opencode-consilium`, `pypi-publish.yml`; leave the environment blank unless the job declares it. |

# Scheduling Consilium audits

`consilium audit --since <ref>` reviews `<ref>...HEAD`, runs the council, saves run artifacts,
and exits `3` when the gate fails. There is no daemon: cron, Task Scheduler, launchd, or CI starts
an ordinary CLI process; no hosted Consilium service or paid Consilium plan is involved. For
uncommitted changes use `consilium --findings --diff --fail-on high "Review the current changes"`.

## Prerequisites

- Node.js 18 or newer, `git`, and a checkout containing the ref you audit (`git fetch --prune`
  first).
- Install the CLI (`npm install --global lv24-opencode-consilium@1.12.1`) or use
  `npx -y lv24-opencode-consilium@1.12.1`. Pin a release you tested; `latest` makes scheduled
  results change under you. The npx examples use `1.12.1` as the pinned placeholder.
- OpenCode must be installed and authenticated: run `opencode auth login`, or provide provider
  keys such as `OPENCODE_API_KEY` or `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` in the scheduler environment. Commit a
  `consilium.config.json` so the same models run every night; verify it with `consilium doctor`.
- `audit --fail-on` enables structured findings automatically; a plain `run` with `--fail-on`
  also needs `--findings` (or `findings: true` in the config). The default `none` never gates.
- Exit codes: `0` passed, `1` run failed, `2` usage/setup error, `3` policy gate failed (new
  findings at or above the threshold). Treat `1` and `2` as failures too, not "no findings".
- Run from the repository root. A full `audit` run writes `.consilium/runs`; add
  `--report sarif --report-file consilium-audit.sarif` (or `--report pr`) for a report.
- `--deadline` is milliseconds (maximum 24 hours; `900000` is 15 minutes). `--max-cost` is a
  soft USD cap based on provider-reported usage.

## Choosing the `--since` ref

| Ref | Example | Use it for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `origin/main` | `--since origin/main` | Feature branches and pre-merge audits after a fetch. |
| Date-based tag | `--since audit/2026-11-01` | Nightly audits of a long-lived branch; tag the last reviewed commit and move it only after success. |
| Recent history | `--since HEAD~20` | A sliding window on a laptop or a repo without tags. |

`audit` uses a three-dot diff from the merge base; on the default branch `origin/main...HEAD` is
empty when `HEAD` equals `origin/main`, so use a tag or `HEAD~N`. Diffs are capped at 60,000 chars.

## cron (Linux and macOS)

Add this with `crontab -e` (cron uses local time unless your cron supports `CRON_TZ`). It runs at
03:00, appends to a log, and preserves the CLI exit code:

```cron
SHELL=/bin/bash
PATH=/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin
0 3 * * * cd /srv/app && git fetch --prune --quiet origin && /usr/local/bin/consilium audit --since origin/main --fail-on high --deadline 900000 --max-cost 2.00 --report pr --report-file consilium-audit.md >> /var/log/consilium-audit.log 2>&1
```

`examples/consilium-audit.sh` adds a timestamped log, a `CONSILIUM_SINCE` override, and a lock.
Cron gives the job a minimal environment: use absolute paths, export provider keys in the wrapper
or a sourced file, and keep logs outside the checkout (or in gitignored `.consilium/logs`).

## Windows Task Scheduler

`examples/consilium-audit.ps1` is the wrapper. Register it once in PowerShell:

```powershell

  -Argument ('-NoLogo -NoProfile -NonInteractive -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "{0}" -RepoDir "{1}"' -f $script, $repo)
$trigger = New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -Daily -At '03:00'
$settings = New-ScheduledTaskSettingsSet -StartWhenAvailable `
  -MultipleInstances IgnoreNew -ExecutionTimeLimit (New-TimeSpan -Minutes 30)
```

The wrapper runs `consilium audit --since origin/main --fail-on high --deadline 900000` (plus a

`.consilium\logs`, and exits with the CLI code. Set `-Consilium` to the absolute `consilium.cmd`
path if the task cannot see npm's global bin directory; `*>> C:\logs\consilium-audit.log` is a
quick manual alternative. Register under the account that owns the OpenCode login; add

## GitHub Actions

`examples/consilium-audit-nightly.yml` is a complete workflow. It deliberately lives under
`examples/`: GitHub only runs files in `.github/workflows/`, and this repository does not enable
it. Copy it to `.github/workflows/` in your repository and review secrets and permissions. It
installs OpenCode, runs the published npm package (not the local composite action), checks out
with `fetch-depth: 0`, and uses `contents: read`. Set the optional `CONSILIUM_SINCE` repository
variable to a tag or `HEAD~20` for real nightly coverage on the default branch:

```yaml
on:
  schedule: [{ cron: '0 3 * * *' }]   # UTC
  workflow_dispatch:
permissions: { contents: read }
concurrency: { group: consilium-audit, cancel-in-progress: false }
# see the example for checkout, setup-node, artifact upload, and gate steps
run: >-
  npx -y lv24-opencode-consilium@1.12.1 audit
  --since "origin/${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }}"
  --fail-on high --deadline 900000 --max-cost 2.00
  --report sarif --report-file consilium-audit.sarif
```

The workflow captures the CLI exit code, uploads `.consilium/runs` and the SARIF 2.1.0 report
with `actions/upload-artifact`, then re-exits with that code. Use `--report pr --report-file
consilium-audit.md` instead if you want a human-readable report; older releases without SARIF
support need the Markdown form. Scheduled workflows run only from the default branch; in a fork
they stay disabled until enabled, and secrets are not copied from the parent repository. Fork
pull requests never receive the base repository's secrets. Keep this schedule on trusted code
and never check out an untrusted fork with secrets present.

## Operating notes

- **Avoid duplicate runs.** Use a concurrency group, a file lock, cron overlap checks, or Task
  Scheduler `MultipleInstances IgnoreNew`. Do not cancel an audit mid-run to start the next one.
- **Keep artifacts, not noise.** `.consilium/runs` holds `run.json`, `report.md`, and per-expert
  files. Retain them for trends and `baseline accept`, but do not commit them. Logs and reports
  contain source diffs and model output; restrict access and set a retention period.
- **Cap cost and time.** Start with free models, set `--max-cost` and `--deadline`, and remember
  that `--max-cost` cannot cap a provider that does not report usage. Set a job timeout too.
- **Alert on failure.** Cron's `MAILTO` only sees unredirected output, so mail the wrapper's
  nonzero status yourself (or leave stderr unredirected). GitHub sends failure notifications and
  Task Scheduler keeps a history. Never map `3` to `0`.
- **Accept known findings deliberately.** Review a run, then run `consilium baseline accept latest`
  (or `accept <runId> --dry-run` first). Commit `.consilium/baseline.json` if the team shares it;
  otherwise every scheduled run starts empty. See [`github-action.md`](github-action.md).

## 3. Рекомендация для Consilium: `--session`

### 3.1. Текущее состояние кода (проверено чтением)

| Место | Факт |
|---|---|
| `src/domain/types.ts` | `ConsiliumConfig.session?: string` — «Переиспользовать сессию OpenCode» |
| `src/domain/types.ts` | `RunOptions.session?: string` |
| `src/interfaces/cli/args.ts` | CLI принимает `--session` |
| `src/infrastructure/opencode/args.ts` | `buildRunArgs` умеет `--session=<id>` с проверкой `SESSION_PATTERN` (`src/domain/council/sessions.ts`) |
| `src/infrastructure/opencode/spawn.ts` | `runAgentProcess` **не передаёт** `session` в `buildRunArgs` |
| `src/infrastructure/opencode/stream.ts` | `sessionID` из событий не извлекается |

То есть опция объявлена, но **не подключена**: сейчас `--session` до `opencode run` не доходит.

### 3.2. Точный маппинг флагов

| Опция Consilium | Аргумент CLI | Когда использовать |
|---|---|---|
| `session: <id>` | `--session=<id>` | Явное продолжение существующей сессии |
| `session: 'auto'` (новая политика) | без флага, затем взять `sessionID` из первого события | Значение по умолчанию: новая сессия на запуск |
| `forkSession: true` | `--fork` (вместе с `--session`) | Ветвление уже накопленного контекста |
| `archiveSession: true` | `--archived` | Только как пометка в данных; **не** скрывает из `session list` |
| `standalone: true` (уже дефолт) | `--standalone` (`src/infrastructure/opencode/args.ts`, `buildRunArgs`) | Обязательно сохранить: плагин работает внутри сервера OpenCode, а дочерние прогоны не должны в него переиспользовать |
| `title: <строка>` | `--title "consilium: <preset>: <короткая задача>"` | Навигация в списке сессий |

Формат id: `ses_` + `[a-z0-9]` (проверено на цифровом id). Не использовать `:` `/` `#` в самостоятельно
сгенерированных id, даже если `SESSION_PATTERN` их допускает: поведение CLI/TUI для них не проверялось.

### 3.3. Политика: новая сессия на запуск, переиспользование — opt-in

**По умолчанию** — новая сессия на каждый `run()`:

* контекст не растёт между запусками (см. 3.4);
* нет конфликтов между параллельными экспертами (T6);
* `sessionID` фиксируется из первого события и пишется в `ConsiliumResult.metadata.sessionID` — этого достаточно,
  чтобы потом явно продолжить (`--session <id>`).

**Opt-in переиспользование** — только **per-expert**, не общая сессия:

```text
ses_consilium_<projectSlug>_<expert>     # у каждого эксперта своя нить
ses_consilium_<projectSlug>_chair        # у председателя своя
```

Почему per-expert: эксперты запускаются параллельно (`callExpertsParallel`), а параллельный запуск на одной сессии
теряет часть промптов (T6). Отдельные id полностью снимают конфликт и дают каждому эксперту собственный
накопленный контекст между раундами.

Продолжение «как было» — через `--fork`, если нужно ответвление без порчи основной нити (T4).

### 3.4. Ловушки

1. **Рост контекста.** Первый ход «Reply with exactly: OK» — `input 16226`; второй ход в той же сессии —
   `input 134 + cache.read 17649`. То есть промпт вырос примерно на 1.5k токенов при ответе в два токена.
   В реальном Consilium каждый ход добавляет промпт эксперта + ответ; при переиспользовании рост линейный и
   упирается в контекстное окно дешёвых моделей. Кэш удешевляет токены, но окно не расширяет.
2. **Архивные сессии не скрываются** из `opencode session list` (T5). Не строить на `--archived` гарантий
   «чистого» списка; для уборки — `opencode session delete`.
3. **Конкурентность.** Одна сессия — один писатель (T6). Никогда не передавать общий `--session` параллельным
   экспертам.
4. **`--continue`** продолжает «последнюю» сессию и в автоматизации опасен: зависит от того, что делал пользователь.
5. **Сессии привязаны к проекту.** `session list` — «in the current project»; в записи есть `directory`
   (наблюдалось `"directory":"C:\\0project\\opencode-consilium"`). При запуске из другого каталога id не найдётся.
6. **Плагин внутри сервера.** Инструмент плагина выполняется в процессе сервера OpenCode. Нельзя использовать
   `sessionID` вызывающей сессии (`ToolContext.sessionID`) для прогонов совета: ответы совета смешаются с ходом
   агента-вызывающего. Только `--standalone` + отдельные id.

### 5.5. Почему только V2

2. Ключ конфига и формат записи различаются (`plugin` + кортеж против `plugins` + объект), автоматическая
   нормализация покрывает конфиг, но не код.
3. Используемые API — `Plugin.define`, `ctx.tool.transform`, `options.codemode`/`namespace`, `ctx.options`,
   `ToolContext.signal` — существуют только в V2.
4. Целевая версия зафиксирована: установленный OpenCode — v2.2.6.

Если позже понадобится V1, документация даёт безопасный способ: экспортировать объект, развернув `Plugin.define`

```ts
  async server() {
    return { /* V1 hooks */ }
  },
}
```

V1 вызовет `server()`, V2 прочитает `id`/`setup` и проигнорирует `server()`.

## P2 — product roadmap (1.6+)

Theme: **from advice to gate** — structured findings, a baseline policy and an
eval harness that proves the council catches more than one model.

### 1. Structured findings contract + dissent ledger (M)

Experts end with a validated `findings[]` block (severity, category, file, line,
claim, evidence, confidence). Merge by stable fingerprint, vote across roles,
keep `contested`; persist the minority positions and render “rejected and why”
in the chair section and reports. Fall back to prose on parse failure.

**Why first:** unlocks gates, inline PR comments, SARIF, comparable runs, and
gives the council's disagreement a product surface. Reuses `prompts.ts`,
`run.ts`, `consensus.ts`, `report.ts`, artifacts.

### 2. Baseline + policy gate (S/M)

`.consilium/baseline.json` with line-independent fingerprints; `--fail-on
high|medium|any`; `baseline accept|prune`; wire into `hooks install` and the PR
report. Makes the existing pre-commit hook enforceable instead of “anything
failed”.

### 3. `consilium eval` harness (M)

20–30 fixtures with planted bugs and clean hunks; deterministic must-catch /
must-not-flag signatures (no LLM judging); report catch rate, false positives,
contested rate, latency and cost per model set. Publish the table in the README.
This is the evidence the product needs.
